The uterine chorion surface is covered with flaky yellow exudate, and abortion occurs in the last month of gestation in sheep.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Brucella ovis; epididymitis is wrong — this describes a male reproductive lesion, not the placental disease of ewes.
  • Campylobacter foetus; oedematous cotyledons is wrong — Campylobacter causes late abortion with haematomas, a distinct pathogen.
  • Coxiella burnetii; interstitial pneumonia is wrong — this describes human Q fever lung pathology, not ovine abortion.
Know More
  • The disease also occurs in goats and has zoonotic importance.
  • Cytoplasmic elementary bodies are seen in tissue sections.
  • Chlamydia psittaci also causes chlamydial abortion in cattle.
  • Other chlamydial diseases include feline pneumonitis and follicular conjunctivitis.

posts.post_title: In classification of fungal diseases, which…
posts.post_content: In classification of fungal diseases, which group of fungi are the only true obligate parasites, living in the keratin layer to cause ringworm?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Dermatophytes

Dermatophytes are the only obligate parasitic fungi, restricted to the keratin layer of skin, causing ringworm (superficial mycosis).

Correct Option Explanation

Because they remain non-invasive within keratin, dermatophyte infections do not produce granulomas, unlike deep mycoses.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Deep/systemic mycoses fungi is wrong — organisms like Histoplasma and Coccidioides establish in normal individuals and form granulomas.
  • Mycetoma-causing saprophytes is wrong — these enter through skin in debilitated hosts, unlike the obligate dermatophytes.
  • Yeasts is wrong — yeasts like Candida and Cryptococcus are not obligate keratin parasites and are of low pathogenicity.
Know More
  • Microsporum shows fluorescence under UV (Wood's lamp) light.
  • Trichophyton grows both within (endothrix) and outside (ectothrix) the hair shaft.
  • Favus produces a 'honeycomb' appearance from Trichophyton schoenleinii.
  • Splendore-Hoeppli material can surround fungal colonies in tissue.

posts.post_title: Aspergillosis in poultry is also known by wh…
posts.post_content: Aspergillosis in poultry is also known by which synonym reflecting its common occurrence in young chicks?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Brooder pneumonia

Aspergillosis in poultry is called 'Brooder pneumonia' because it is common in chicks raised in brooders.

Correct Option Explanation

It is caused by Aspergillus fumigatus, producing greyish pulmonary nodules with central bluish mycelial material.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Turkey X disease is wrong — this historic name refers to aflatoxicosis outbreaks in turkeys, not aspergillosis.
  • Favus is wrong — this is a dermatophytosis causing a 'honeycomb' skin lesion, unrelated to Aspergillus pneumonia.
  • Facial eczema is wrong — this is caused by the mycotoxin sporidesmin from Pithomyces chartarum.
Know More
  • Eggs can be invaded by the fungus, causing chicks to hatch infected.
  • Special stains like PAS demonstrate club-like conidiospores.
  • Cattle placentitis due to Aspergillus can cause abortion.
  • Granulomas show central caseation with fibrous capsules.

posts.post_title: Aflatoxins, responsible for aflatoxicosis, a…
posts.post_content: Aflatoxins, responsible for aflatoxicosis, are produced by which fungi?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Aspergillus flavus and A. parasiticus

Aflatoxins are produced by Aspergillus flavus and A. parasiticus, contaminating groundnuts, maize and cottonseed.

Correct Option Explanation

Aflatoxin B1 is the most prevalent and toxic type, and it causes a specific G-to-T transversion mutation in codon 249 of the p53 gene.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Fusarium roseum is wrong — this fungus produces zearalenone, an oestrogenic mycotoxin, not aflatoxin.
  • Claviceps purpurea is wrong — this fungus produces ergot alkaloids, causing ergotism.
  • Pithomyces chartarum is wrong — this fungus produces sporidesmin, causing facial eczema.
Know More
  • 'Turkey X disease' (1961) led to aflatoxin's chemical identification.
  • Aflatoxin M1 is a milk-excreted metabolite of B1.
  • Acute aflatoxicosis causes centrilobular necrosis in pigs, cattle and dogs.
  • Chronic exposure produces bile ductule proliferation and cirrhosis.

posts.post_title: Ergotism, caused by Claviceps purpurea, clas…
posts.post_content: Ergotism, caused by Claviceps purpurea, classically produces which gangrenous change in the gangrenous form?

_aimcq_options.text: Dry gangrene of the limbs, tail and ears
Wet gangrene of the udder only

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Dry gangrene of the limbs, tail and ears

The gangrenous form of ergotism causes dry gangrene of the distal limbs, tail and ears after weeks of ingesting contaminated grain.

Correct Option Explanation

Ergot alkaloids (ergotamine, ergocristine) cause prolonged vascular smooth-muscle contraction, cutting off blood supply to distal extremities.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Wet gangrene of udder only is wrong — udder/teat lesions are typical of facial eczema, while ergotism affects limbs, tail and ears.
  • Gangrene of tongue only is wrong — ergotism in birds affects the comb, tongue and beak, but mammalian ergotism centres on the limbs.
  • No gangrene, only convulsions is wrong — this describes the separate, rarer spasmodic (convulsive) form of ergotism.
Know More
  • The spasmodic form causes opisthotonus and tetanic convulsions.
  • Ergot's oxytocic action on the uterus can cause abortion.
  • Gangrenous ergotism resembles fescue poisoning grossly.
  • Agalactia may be the only sign seen in pigs.

posts.post_title: Facial Eczema of sheep results from hepatoto…
posts.post_content: Facial Eczema of sheep results from hepatotoxic photosensitization caused by which mycotoxin?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Sporidesmin

Facial Eczema results from sporidesmin, a mycotoxin produced by Pithomyces chartarum growing on ryegrass pastures.

Correct Option Explanation

Sporidesmin damages the liver, causing failure to clear phylloerythrin, which accumulates and causes photosensitization of the face and ears.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Aflatoxin B1 is wrong — this causes hepatic necrosis and carcinoma, not the classic photosensitization syndrome of facial eczema.
  • Zearalenone is wrong — this Fusarium toxin causes oestrogenic disease in pigs, unrelated to facial eczema.
  • Ochratoxin A is wrong — this causes nephrotoxicity ('mouldy nephrosis'), not hepatotoxic photosensitization.
Know More
  • Was first described in sheep in New Zealand.
  • In cattle, the udder and teats are the most affected sites.
  • Microscopic lesion is cholangio-hepatitis with biliary epithelial necrosis.
  • Focal hepatic necrosis with regenerative hyperplasia may occur.

posts.post_title: Zearalenone, an oestrogenic mycotoxin produc…
posts.post_content: Zearalenone, an oestrogenic mycotoxin produced by Fusarium species, mainly affects which species and organ system?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Sows; reproductive tract, causing vulvovaginitis

Zearalenone (F-2 toxin) mainly causes vulvovaginitis in sows by stimulating oestrus and producing reproductive tract enlargement.

Correct Option Explanation

It causes ovarian follicular atresia, uterine oedema, and in young males, feminization with testicular atrophy and gynaecomastia.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Horses; cerebral white matter is wrong — cerebral leukomalacia is caused by a different fungal mycotoxin (mouldy corn poisoning), not zearalenone.
  • Cattle; udder photosensitization is wrong — this describes facial eczema caused by sporidesmin.
  • Poultry; respiratory tract is wrong — respiratory mycotoxin disease is typical of Aspergillus (brooder pneumonia), not zearalenone.
Know More
  • Zearalenone is produced by Fusarium roseum and related species.
  • It contaminates maize primarily.
  • Ingestion in early pregnancy can cause embryonic death.
  • Reduced fertility in cattle is also suspected from this toxin.

posts.post_title: The characteristic 'pipe stem' or 'clay pipe…
posts.post_content: The characteristic 'pipe stem' or 'clay pipe' appearance of the liver in chronic Fascioliasis results from which process?

_aimcq_options.text: Fibrosis and calcification of the bile ducts
Deposition of amyloid in portal triads

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Fibrosis and calcification of the bile ducts

The 'pipe stem' or 'clay pipe' liver of chronic fascioliasis results from fibrosis and calcification of the bile ducts.

Correct Option Explanation

Chronic irritation by adult Fasciola hepatica/gigantica flukes causes cholangiohepatitis with biliary epithelial hyperplasia and progressive duct wall thickening.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Amyloid deposition is wrong — amyloidosis is unrelated to fluke-induced bile duct pathology.
  • Granulomatous hepatitis from Ascaris is wrong — Ascaris larvae migrating in the liver instead cause 'milk spot' lesions, not pipe stem change.
  • Aflatoxin necrosis is wrong — this is a toxic, not parasitic, cause of centrilobular hepatic necrosis.
Know More
  • The intermediate host of Fasciola is the snail Lymnaea.
  • Fascioloides magna wanders in the peritoneal cavity before invading the liver.
  • Ova are oval, pedunculated and golden brown.
  • Chronic disease presents with anaemia and submandibular oedema.

posts.post_title: Hydatid disease (echinococcosis) is caused b…
posts.post_content: Hydatid disease (echinococcosis) is caused by the larval stage of which tapeworm genus, with dogs as the definitive host?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Echinococcus

Hydatid disease is caused by larval cysts of Echinococcus tapeworms, with dogs and wild carnivores as definitive hosts.

Correct Option Explanation

E. granulosus larvae occur in sheep, cattle and other intermediate hosts, forming cysts mainly in the liver and lungs.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Taenia is wrong — Taenia species produce cysticerci (e.g. C. cellulosae, C. bovis), not hydatid cysts.
  • Moniezia is wrong — this tapeworm causes moniezisis in ruminants without a bladder-worm larval stage of concern here.
  • Multiceps is wrong — this genus's larva, Coenurus cerebralis, causes 'Gid' in sheep, a distinct condition.
Know More
  • E. multilocularis uses foxes/dogs/cats as final hosts and rodents as intermediates.
  • Cysticercus cellulosae in pigs produces 'measly pork'.
  • Coenurus cerebralis causes 'Gid' in sheep via dog tapeworm M. multiceps.
  • Diagnosis includes complement fixation and haemagglutination tests.

posts.post_title: In horses, Strongylus vulgaris larvae charac…
posts.post_content: In horses, Strongylus vulgaris larvae characteristically migrate into which vessel, producing verminous aneurysm?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Anterior (cranial) mesenteric artery

Strongylus vulgaris larvae migrate into the anterior (cranial) mesenteric artery, producing thrombosis and verminous aneurysm.

Correct Option Explanation

This can extend to the aorta and iliac arteries, causing hind-limb weakness and severe abdominal pain from vascular occlusion.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Pulmonary artery is wrong — this site is classically affected by Dirofilaria immitis in dogs, not S. vulgaris in horses.
  • Portal vein is wrong — this is a site for Schistosoma bovis/haematobium obstruction, not S. vulgaris.
  • Jugular vein is wrong — this vessel is not the migratory site described for S. vulgaris.
Know More
  • S. vulgaris is a double-toothed strongyle.
  • S. equinus is triple-toothed and forms nodular 'worm nests' in the caecal wall.
  • S. edentatus larvae encyst in the abdominal wall before reaching serosa.
  • Verminous enteritis is a common associated lesion.

posts.post_title: Which hookworm species affects cattle, causi…
posts.post_content: Which hookworm species affects cattle, causing bunostomiasis with anasarca and severe anaemia?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Bunostomum phlebotomum

Bunostomum phlebotomum is the hookworm causing bunostomiasis in cattle, with anasarca and severe blood-loss anaemia.

Correct Option Explanation

Calves aged 4–12 months are most affected, especially in winter, with worms concentrated in the first few feet of small intestine.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Ancylostoma caninum is wrong — this hookworm affects dogs and cats, not cattle.
  • Haemonchus contortus is wrong — this is an abomasal blood-sucking worm of sheep, goats and cattle, but is not a hookworm (family Trichostrongyloidea).
  • Bunostomum trigonocephalum is wrong — this species affects sheep, not cattle.
Know More
  • Over 2000 worms indicate a likely fatal infestation level in calves.
  • Prepatent period of B. phlebotomum is about 8 months.
  • Larvae penetrate skin and migrate via lungs before reaching the intestine.
  • Diagnosis relies on blunt, pigmented hookworm eggs in faeces.

posts.post_title: Haemonchus contortus, the 'barber's pole wor…
posts.post_content: Haemonchus contortus, the 'barber's pole worm', is found in which organ and produces what characteristic clinical sign?

_aimcq_options.text: Abomasum; anaemia with submandibular oedema ('bottle jaw')

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Abomasum; anaemia with submandibular oedema ('bottle jaw')

Haemonchus contortus resides in the abomasum of sheep, goats and cattle and produces severe anaemia with submandibular oedema ('bottle jaw').

Correct Option Explanation

It is a blood-sucking nematode that lacerates the mucosa, causing haemorrhage, and a 'self-cure' phenomenon can occur as immunity develops.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Small intestine; steatorrhoea is wrong — Haemonchus resides in the abomasum, and steatorrhoea is not its clinical hallmark.
  • Caecum; tenesmus is wrong — this describes coccidial or strongyle infections of the large bowel, not Haemonchus.
  • Lungs; chronic cough is wrong — lung worm infections, not Haemonchus, cause respiratory signs.
Know More
  • Abomasal mucosa shows shallow ulcers and haemorrhages.
  • Ascites and hydropericardium may accompany severe infection.
  • It belongs to family Trichostrongyloidea.
  • Life cycle is direct with no intermediate host.

posts.post_title: Spirocerca lupi in dogs characteristically f…
posts.post_content: Spirocerca lupi in dogs characteristically forms nodules in which two anatomical sites?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Oesophagus and aorta

Spirocerca lupi forms nodules in the oesophagus and aortic wall of dogs, foxes and cats.

Correct Option Explanation

Aortic nodules can form aneurysms that rupture, causing fatal haemorrhage, while oesophageal nodules may cause obstruction and vomiting.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Bile duct and pancreas is wrong — biliary lesions are typical of liver flukes (Fasciola), not Spirocerca.
  • Lungs and pleura is wrong — pulmonary parasitism is typical of lungworms, not Spirocerca's aorto-oesophageal localisation.
  • Kidney and ureter is wrong — renal parasitism is typical of Dioctophyma renale, not Spirocerca.
Know More
  • Coprophagous beetles serve as the intermediate host.
  • Fibrosarcoma and osteosarcoma have been reported as metastatic complications.
  • Eggs are small, gelatin-capsule shaped with a coiled larva.
  • Exostoses of thoracic vertebrae may occur from aberrant larval migration.

posts.post_title: Dirofilaria immitis, the canine heart worm,…
posts.post_content: Dirofilaria immitis, the canine heart worm, characteristically resides in which cardiac chamber?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Right ventricle

Adult Dirofilaria immitis worms reside in the right ventricle (and pulmonary artery) of dogs, where they may live for years.

Correct Option Explanation

Heavy worm burdens obstruct blood flow, causing right ventricular hypertrophy and chronic venous congestion of liver, spleen and lungs.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Left ventricle is wrong — the parasite localises to the right side of the heart, not the systemic (left) side.
  • Left atrium is wrong — this chamber is not the site of Dirofilaria localisation.
  • Right atrium only is wrong — worms are found mainly in the right ventricle and pulmonary artery, not confined to the atrium.
Know More
  • Mosquitoes are the intermediate hosts and vectors.
  • Dead worms can form emboli causing pulmonary infarction.
  • Immune complex glomerulonephritis is a recognised complication.
  • Diagnosis includes demonstration of microfilaria in peripheral blood.

posts.post_title: Setaria digitata, normally a peritoneal para…
posts.post_content: Setaria digitata, normally a peritoneal parasite of cattle, causes which serious condition when it aberrantly invades the CNS of sheep, goats or horses?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Cerebrospinal nematodiasis (lumbar paralysis / kumri)

Aberrant CNS invasion by Setaria digitata causes cerebrospinal nematodiasis, known as lumbar paralysis in sheep/goats and 'kumri' in horses.

Correct Option Explanation

Immature worms wander randomly through the brain, leaving necrotic tracks with haemorrhage, gitter cells and eosinophilic infiltration.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Negri bodies encephalitis is wrong — Negri bodies are a viral (rabies) inclusion, unrelated to this nematode disease.
  • Coenurosis (Gid) is wrong — this is caused by the larval tapeworm Coenurus cerebralis, a cestode, not Setaria.
  • Visceral larval migrans is wrong — this term applies to aberrant ascarid larval migration, not Setaria.
Know More
  • Setaria's normal habitat is the peritoneal cavity of cattle.
  • The disease is prevalent in India.
  • Young horses aged 1–2 years show swaying/wobbling gait.
  • Bilateral symmetrical areas of malacia occur in the CNS.

posts.post_title: Which coccidian species is considered most p…
posts.post_content: Which coccidian species is considered most pathogenic in poultry, mainly affecting the caecum?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Eimeria tenella

Eimeria tenella is the most pathogenic coccidian of poultry, affecting the caecum and causing high mortality.

Correct Option Explanation

The coccidial life cycle involves oocyst ingestion, asexual schizogony producing merozoites, and sexual gametogony forming new oocysts shed in faeces.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Eimeria necatrix is wrong — this species affects the small intestine of fowl, not primarily the caecum.
  • Eimeria stiedae is wrong — this species affects the intrahepatic bile ducts of rabbits, not poultry caecum.
  • Eimeria truncata is wrong — this species affects the renal tubules of geese, unrelated to poultry caecal disease.
Know More
  • Mortality from poultry coccidiosis may reach 90–100%.
  • E. stiedae causes hepatic nodules with adenomatous-like hyperplasia in rabbits.
  • E. zurnii and E. bovis affect the caecum, colon and ileum of cattle.
  • Diagnosis relies on demonstrating oocysts in faeces.

posts.post_title: Babesia bigemina, the most common cause of b…
posts.post_content: Babesia bigemina, the most common cause of bovine babesiosis in India, is transmitted by which tick and appears in erythrocytes in what form?

_aimcq_options.text: Boophilus annulatus; pear-shaped forms in pairs

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Boophilus annulatus; pear-shaped forms in pairs

Babesia bigemina is transmitted by the tick Boophilus annulatus and appears in erythrocytes as pear-shaped forms in pairs.

Correct Option Explanation

It causes bovine piroplasmosis (Texas fever, red water) with fever, haemoglobinuria and haemolytic anaemia.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Ixodes ricinus; ring forms singly is wrong — Ixodes ricinus is linked to tick-borne fever (Ehrlichia), not B. bigemina's classic paired form.
  • Rhipicephalus sanguineus; rod-shaped chains is wrong — this tick is the vector for canine ehrlichiosis, and Babesia is not rod-shaped.
  • Dermacentor sp.; comma-shaped is wrong — this is not the vector or morphology described for B. bigemina.
Know More
  • Bos indicus breeds show relative resistance due to tick resistance.
  • Babesia fully catabolises haemoglobin, unlike Plasmodium's haemozoin pigment.
  • Equine babesiosis is caused by B. caballi and the more pathogenic B. equi.
  • Canine babesiosis is caused by B. canis and B. gibsoni.

posts.post_title: The pathognomonic 'Koch's blue bodies' seen…
posts.post_content: The pathognomonic 'Koch's blue bodies' seen in lymph node biopsies are diagnostic of which disease?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Theileriosis

Koch's blue bodies, representing schizonts in lymphocytes and monocytes, are pathognomonic of Theileriosis.

Correct Option Explanation

The disease is caused by Theileria species (e.g. T. annulata in India) transmitted by ticks, producing high fever and lymph node swelling.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Babesiosis is wrong — Babesia organisms appear as pear-shaped forms within erythrocytes, not as Koch's blue bodies in lymphocytes.
  • Anaplasmosis is wrong — Anaplasma appears as a coccoid form at the erythrocyte periphery, unrelated to Koch's blue bodies.
  • Trypanosomiasis is wrong — Trypanosomes are extracellular flagellates in plasma, not intracellular schizonts forming blue bodies.
Know More
  • T. parva causes East Coast Fever in Africa, not recorded in India.
  • T. mutans occurs in India without producing clinical symptoms.
  • Abomasal punched-out ulcers are a described gross lesion.
  • Cytotoxic CD8+ cells kill infected lymphoblasts in immune animals.

posts.post_title: Surra, an acute or chronic disease of equine…
posts.post_content: Surra, an acute or chronic disease of equines and camels, is caused by which trypanosome?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Trypanosoma evansi

Surra is caused by Trypanosoma evansi, and the disease is always fatal in camels and horses.

Correct Option Explanation

Progressive anaemia and hypoglycaemia occur as the parasite consumes host glucose, along with splenic and lymph node hyperplasia.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • T. equiperdum is wrong — this causes Dourine, a venereally transmitted equine disease with genital lesions.
  • T. cruzi is wrong — this causes Chaga's disease, affecting the brain and myocardium in humans, dogs and cats.
  • T. brucei is wrong — this causes Nagana, African trypanosomiasis of domestic animals via tsetse flies.
Know More
  • Mal de caderas is a similar acute trypanosome disease of horses.
  • T. congolense and T. vivax cause wasting disease in cattle.
  • Trypanosomes evade immunity via variable surface glycoproteins (VSGs).
  • Diagnosis relies on blood smear examination in the acute phase.

posts.post_title: Toxoplasma gondii completes its sexual cycle…
posts.post_content: Toxoplasma gondii completes its sexual cycle in which definitive host?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Cat

The cat is the definitive host of Toxoplasma gondii, where the parasite's sexual cycle and oocyst formation occur.

Correct Option Explanation

Cats become infected by ingesting infected meat or sporulated oocysts; other species act as intermediate hosts via tissue cysts.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Dog is wrong — dogs are not the definitive host of Toxoplasma; toxoplasmosis in dogs is more common in puppies with distemper co-infection.
  • Sheep is wrong — sheep are intermediate hosts, showing abortion and placental necrosis, not the definitive host.
  • Pig is wrong — pigs, like sheep, act only as intermediate hosts for this parasite.
Know More
  • Congenital infection of lambs/kids causes encephalitis.
  • In cats, manifestations include pneumonia, encephalitis and pancreatitis.
  • Toxoplasma has major zoonotic importance.
  • Diagnosis uses CFT, ELISA and indirect fluorescent antibody test.

posts.post_title: Vitamin A deficiency in the respiratory trac…
posts.post_content: Vitamin A deficiency in the respiratory tract causes which epithelial change?

_aimcq_options.text: Metaplasia of ciliated columnar epithelium to stratified squamous epithelium

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Metaplasia of ciliated columnar epithelium to stratified squamous epithelium

Vitamin A deficiency converts the ciliated columnar respiratory epithelium into keratinised stratified squamous epithelium.

Correct Option Explanation

This metaplastic change removes protective mucus and cilia, predisposing to secondary infection, and similar metaplasia occurs in the urinary tract.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Atrophy without metaplasia is wrong — the hallmark lesion is specifically squamous metaplasia, not simple atrophy.
  • Goblet cell hyperplasia only is wrong — vitamin A deficiency actually reduces mucus-secreting cells rather than increasing them.
  • Squamous cell carcinoma is wrong — this is a neoplastic change, not the metaplastic lesion of hypovitaminosis A.
Know More
  • In the urinary tract, transitional epithelium similarly becomes squamous, predisposing to calculi.
  • Xerophthalmia results from keratinisation of corneal/scleral membranes.
  • Night blindness (nyctalopia) results from impaired retinal aldehyde function.
  • In bulls, deficiency causes sterility and abortion in females.

posts.post_title: In calves, severe Vitamin A deficiency retar…
posts.post_content: In calves, severe Vitamin A deficiency retards skull bone growth, leading to which neurological consequence?

_aimcq_options.text: Brain herniation into the foramen with blindness from optic nerve pressure
Demyelination of the spinal cord white matter

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Brain herniation into the foramen with blindness from optic nerve pressure

Vitamin A deficiency in calves retards skull growth while the brain continues to grow, causing herniation into the foramen and optic nerve compression leading to blindness.

Correct Option Explanation

The deficiency halts capillary invasion of cartilage and osteoblastic activity, impairing endochondral bone growth broadly.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Cerebellar hypoplasia is wrong — this is a viral lesion of Feline Panleucopenia or BVD, not vitamin A deficiency.
  • Non-suppurative encephalitis is wrong — this is an inflammatory viral lesion pattern, not a nutritional bone-growth defect.
  • Demyelination is wrong — this describes lesions of Visna or Scrapie, not vitamin A deficiency.
Know More
  • Birds show hydrocephalus from defective bone growth.
  • Poultry 'nutritional roup' shows caseous material in eyes and nostrils.
  • Congenital anomalies include cleft palate and micro-ophthalmos.
  • Vitamin A is stored mainly in hepatic Kupffer cells as retinol.

posts.post_title: Rickets, the classical Vitamin D deficiency…
posts.post_content: Rickets, the classical Vitamin D deficiency disease of young animals, is characterized by which skeletal change?

_aimcq_options.text: Failure of mineralisation of osteoid at growth plates, producing bowed legs

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Failure of mineralisation of osteoid at growth plates, producing bowed legs

Rickets results from failure of osteoid mineralisation at growing bone ends, producing bowed legs and enlarged costochondral junctions ('rickety rosary').

Correct Option Explanation

Vitamin D deficiency reduces intestinal calcium absorption, so osteoid matrix is laid down but not properly calcified.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Excess mineralisation of soft tissue is wrong — this describes metastatic calcification, seen in hypervitaminosis D, not deficiency.
  • Osteosclerosis is wrong — rickets causes bone softening, not increased density.
  • Absence of osteoid formation is wrong — osteoid is still formed in rickets, but it fails to mineralise properly.
Know More
  • Adult rickets is called osteomalacia.
  • Poultry show thin-shelled eggs and a pliable beak.
  • Vitamin D2 (calciferol) derives from ergosterol; D3 (cholecalciferol) from 7-dehydrocholesterol.
  • Excess lush green feed can antagonise vitamin D due to vitamin A's anti-D activity.

posts.post_title: Hypervitaminosis D produces which pathologic…
posts.post_content: Hypervitaminosis D produces which pathological change?

_aimcq_options.text: Hypercalcaemia with metastatic calcification and renal damage

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Hypercalcaemia with metastatic calcification and renal damage

Hypervitaminosis D causes hypercalcaemia and hypercalciuria, leading to metastatic calcification and renal damage.

Correct Option Explanation

Excess osteoclastic activity from vitamin D toxicity can also cause osteoporosis of bone despite the elevated serum calcium.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Rickets with bowed legs is wrong — this is a deficiency, not excess, state of vitamin D.
  • Osteomalacia is wrong — this adult form of rickets is also caused by deficiency, not excess.
  • Haemorrhagic diathesis is wrong — this is characteristic of vitamin K deficiency, not vitamin D excess.
Know More
  • Milk fever is a related but distinct sudden hypocalcaemia after parturition.
  • Vitamin D is synthesised endogenously in skin from UV light exposure.
  • Sources include fish liver oil and sun-cured hay.
  • Deficiency is more common in animals housed indoors in winter.

posts.post_title: Vitamin E deficiency in calves and lambs cla…
posts.post_content: Vitamin E deficiency in calves and lambs classically produces which condition?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 'White muscle disease' (nutritional muscular dystrophy)

Vitamin E deficiency in calves and lambs causes 'White muscle disease', also called 'stiff lamb disease' in lambs.

Correct Option Explanation

Vitamin E acts as a natural antioxidant protecting cell membranes and unsaturated fatty acids; its deficiency leads to muscle necrosis.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Rickets is wrong — this is caused by vitamin D deficiency, affecting bone mineralisation, not muscle.
  • Scurvy is wrong — this is caused by vitamin C deficiency, mainly a human condition affecting collagen.
  • Beri beri is wrong — this is caused by thiamine (B1) deficiency in humans, affecting the nervous system.
Know More
  • Selenium is termed the 'vitamin E sparer' as it enhances its retention.
  • Horses show a related condition called Azoturia.
  • Pigs and minks develop 'yellow fat disease' (steatitis).
  • Poultry show encephalomalacia, called 'crazy chick disease'.

posts.post_title: In poultry, Vitamin E deficiency causing cer…
posts.post_content: In poultry, Vitamin E deficiency causing cerebellar damage with ataxia and torticollis is known as:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Encephalomalacia (crazy chick disease)

Encephalomalacia, or 'crazy chick disease', is a Vitamin E deficiency condition in chicks around 5 weeks of age.

Correct Option Explanation

It causes cerebellar oedema, haemorrhage and neuronal degeneration, driven by increased polyunsaturated fatty acid peroxidation.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Curled toe paralysis is wrong — this is a riboflavin (B2) deficiency condition, not vitamin E.
  • Perosis is wrong — this slipped-tendon condition relates to manganese deficiency, not vitamin E.
  • Exudative diathesis is wrong — although also linked to vitamin E deficiency, this specific condition involves capillary permeability and oedema, not cerebellar signs.
Know More
  • Exudative diathesis shows damage to capillary endothelial cells with plasma leakage.
  • Nutritional muscular dystrophy in chicks involves sulphur-containing amino acid deficiency.
  • Vitamin E is considered the 'vitamin A sparer' in the gut.
  • Selenium and vitamin E deficiencies often occur together.

posts.post_title: Vitamin K deficiency primarily impairs the f…
posts.post_content: Vitamin K deficiency primarily impairs the formation of which coagulation factors?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Prothrombin and Factor X

Vitamin K deficiency impairs hepatic formation of prothrombin and Factor X, producing a haemorrhagic syndrome.

Correct Option Explanation

Causes include obstructive jaundice (lack of bile for absorption), intestinal disorders, and antibiotic/coccidiostat use suppressing gut bacterial synthesis.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Fibrinogen only is wrong — fibrinogen synthesis is not specifically vitamin K-dependent in this text's description.
  • Factor VIII is wrong — this factor is not vitamin K-dependent; it is linked to haemophilia A in humans.
  • Von Willebrand factor is wrong — this is unrelated to vitamin K-dependent clotting factor synthesis.
Know More
  • Sweet clover poisoning causes vitamin K–responsive decreased prothrombin.
  • Poultry show subcutaneous and abdominal haemorrhages.
  • Vitamin K2 is synthesised by intestinal microflora.
  • Haemorrhages occur during wing banding in deficient chicks.

posts.post_title: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is essential for t…
posts.post_content: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is essential for the formation of which structural proteins?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine (collagen constituents)

Vitamin C is required for the formation of hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine, essential constituents of collagen.

Correct Option Explanation

Deficiency impairs mesenchymal derivatives (osteoid, dentine, collagen), delaying wound healing and weakening capillary intercellular cement substance.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Keratin is wrong — keratin synthesis is more closely linked to biotin, not vitamin C.
  • Myosin is wrong — this muscle protein's synthesis is not vitamin C dependent.
  • Elastin only is wrong — vitamin C's role centres on collagen hydroxylation, not elastin specifically.
Know More
  • Guinea pigs and primates, like humans, cannot synthesise their own vitamin C.
  • Deficiency in humans is called scurvy.
  • 'Battery sickness' in caged birds is linked to this deficiency.
  • Vitamin C also supports adrenal steroid hormone secretion.

posts.post_title: The characteristic 'star gazing attitude' in…
posts.post_content: The characteristic 'star gazing attitude' in poultry, with the bird sitting on flexed legs and head retracted, is seen in deficiency of which vitamin?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Thiamine (Vitamin B1)

The 'star gazing attitude' in poultry results from thiamine (Vitamin B1) deficiency, with polyneuritis and paralysis starting from the toes.

Correct Option Explanation

Thiamine is essential for acetylcholine synthesis; its lack causes degeneration of peripheral nerves and heart muscle atrophy.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Riboflavin is wrong — its deficiency causes 'curled toe paralysis', not the star-gazing posture.
  • Niacin is wrong — deficiency causes dermatitis and diarrhoea (pellagra-like signs), not the star-gazing posture.
  • Pyridoxine is wrong — deficiency causes microcytic anaemia and dermatitis, not the classic thiamine posture.
Know More
  • 'Chastek paralysis' occurs in cats/foxes fed raw fish containing thiaminase.
  • Human thiamine deficiency is called 'Beri Beri'.
  • Pigs show cardiac dilatation and myocardial necrosis.
  • Horses fed bracken fern show incoordination and bradycardia.

posts.post_title: 'Curled toe paralysis' in chicks, with inwar…
posts.post_content: 'Curled toe paralysis' in chicks, with inward curling of toes and swollen sciatic/brachial nerves, results from deficiency of which vitamin?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Riboflavin (Vitamin B2)

'Curled toe paralysis' results from riboflavin (Vitamin B2) deficiency in chicks and poults.

Correct Option Explanation

Sciatic and brachial nerves become swollen and discoloured due to Schwann cell degeneration and proliferation.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Thiamine is wrong — its deficiency causes the 'star gazing attitude', a different neurological posture.
  • Biotin is wrong — biotin deficiency causes dermatitis, footpad fissures and 'fatty liver and kidney syndrome' in birds.
  • Folic acid is wrong — its deficiency causes macrocytic anaemia and feather pigmentation defects, not curled toe paralysis.
Know More
  • Chicks also show clubbed down feathers with riboflavin deficiency.
  • Pigs show conjunctivitis, cataracts and normocytic-normochromic anaemia.
  • Riboflavin is stored in egg yolk.
  • Adults show decreased hatchability and dead-in-shell embryos.

posts.post_title: Niacin (Vitamin B3) deficiency in pigs, call…
posts.post_content: Niacin (Vitamin B3) deficiency in pigs, called 'pig pellagra', is aggravated by which dietary factor?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Increased corn feeding (low tryptophan)

'Pig pellagra' is aggravated by increased corn feeding, since corn is low in tryptophan, the amino acid precursor of niacin.

Correct Option Explanation

Deficiency causes dermatitis, diarrhoea, anaemia and necrotic enteritis with hyperkeratosis and alopecia.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Excess green fodder is wrong — green fodder is not identified as a cause of niacin deficiency.
  • High calcium intake is wrong — calcium excess is linked to zinc deficiency (parakeratosis), not niacin deficiency.
  • Excess vitamin A is wrong — this is unrelated to niacin metabolism in this context.
Know More
  • Human niacin deficiency is called pellagra, with the '3 Ds': dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia.
  • Cats cannot convert tryptophan to niacin.
  • Dogs show 'black tongue' (canine pellagra/Stuttgart's disease).
  • Young birds show perosis-like chondrodystrophy with other deficiencies.

posts.post_title: Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) is a required coenzy…
posts.post_content: Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) is a required coenzyme for the conversion of which amino acid to niacin?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Tryptophan

Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) is required as a coenzyme for the metabolism of tryptophan to niacin.

Correct Option Explanation

Deficiency causes microcytic hypochromic anaemia in pigs, dermatitis, and nervous signs such as ataxia and convulsions in young animals.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Methionine is wrong — this amino acid is instead linked to choline synthesis, not the B6-tryptophan-niacin pathway.
  • Lysine is wrong — this amino acid, with folic acid, is linked to feather pigmentation in poultry, not niacin conversion.
  • Phenylalanine is wrong — this amino acid's metabolism relates to vitamin C, not the B6-niacin pathway.
Know More
  • Deficiency can cause renal tubular regeneration forming calculi.
  • Pyridoxine is required for melanin formation and antibody production.
  • It is also a coenzyme for transaminases and decarboxylases.
  • Sources are largely of plant origin, similar to niacin.

posts.post_title: Pantothenic acid deficiency in pigs produces…
posts.post_content: Pantothenic acid deficiency in pigs produces a characteristic gait described as:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 'Goose stepping gait'

Pantothenic acid deficiency in pigs produces the characteristic 'goose stepping gait', with the animal resting on its hocks.

Correct Option Explanation

Pantothenic acid is essential for Coenzyme A synthesis; deficiency also causes haemorrhagic and necrotic colitis and neuronal necrosis.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • 'Star gazing attitude' is wrong — this describes thiamine (B1) deficiency in poultry, not pantothenic acid deficiency in pigs.
  • 'Wobbling gait' is wrong — this describes Setaria digitata-induced cerebrospinal nematodiasis in young horses ('kumri').
  • 'Bunny hopping gait' is not the term used for pantothenic acid deficiency in this text.
Know More
  • Deficiency is aggravated by increased corn feeding.
  • Ducks develop anaemia since haem synthesis needs pantothenic acid.
  • Copper antagonises pantothenic acid activity.
  • Poultry breeders show reduced egg production and hatchability.

posts.post_title: Biotin deficiency in poultry can cause a met…
posts.post_content: Biotin deficiency in poultry can cause a metabolic disorder in young birds known as:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Fatty liver and kidney syndrome (FLKS)

Biotin deficiency can cause Fatty Liver and Kidney Syndrome (FLKS) in young birds.

Correct Option Explanation

Reduced biotin availability impairs gluconeogenesis, causing hypoglycaemia, nervous tissue damage and fat accumulation in the liver.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Perosis is wrong — this slipped-tendon disorder is primarily linked to manganese deficiency, not biotin alone.
  • Curled toe paralysis is wrong — this is caused by riboflavin deficiency, a different B vitamin.
  • Nutritional roup is wrong — this is a term used for vitamin A deficiency in poultry.
Know More
  • Biotin deficiency also causes dermatitis and beak/footpad fissures.
  • Avidin, found in raw egg white, is an anti-biotin factor.
  • Biotin is synthesised by ruminal microflora.
  • It is essential for keratin (a hard protein) synthesis.

posts.post_title: Folic acid deficiency characteristically cau…
posts.post_content: Folic acid deficiency characteristically causes which type of anaemia?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Macrocytic (megaloblastic) anaemia

Folic acid deficiency causes macrocytic (megaloblastic) anaemia, since folate is essential for nucleic acid synthesis and cell proliferation.

Correct Option Explanation

The haematopoietic system is highly sensitive to folate lack, producing megaloblastic bone marrow changes and leucopenia.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Microcytic hypochromic anaemia is wrong — this pattern is typical of iron or pyridoxine deficiency, not folic acid.
  • Normocytic normochromic anaemia is wrong — this pattern is described for riboflavin deficiency in pigs, not folic acid.
  • Haemolytic anaemia is wrong — this is a destructive process (e.g. in Babesiosis), not the folate-deficiency mechanism.
Know More
  • Pigs cannot synthesise folic acid in their intestine, unlike other species.
  • In poultry, folic acid works with lysine for feather pigmentation.
  • Sulphonamide therapy can precipitate deficiency in poultry.
  • Turkeys show cervical deformity with deficiency.

posts.post_title: Vitamin B12 deficiency requires the absence…
posts.post_content: Vitamin B12 deficiency requires the absence of which gastric factor for its malabsorption to occur?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Intrinsic factor (haemopoietin) from parietal cells

Vitamin B12 malabsorption occurs due to absence of intrinsic factor (haemopoietin), secreted by gastric parietal cells.

Correct Option Explanation

B12, a cobalt-containing vitamin, is essential for thymidine biosynthesis and nucleic acid metabolism, and its deficiency causes pernicious (macrocytic) anaemia.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Pepsin is wrong — pepsin is involved in protein digestion, not specifically B12 absorption via intrinsic factor.
  • Hydrochloric acid alone is wrong — while gastric acid aids release of B12 from food, intrinsic factor is the specific absorption cofactor.
  • Gastrin is wrong — gastrin regulates acid secretion, not B12 absorption directly.
Know More
  • B12 is also called the Animal Protein Factor (APF).
  • Cobalt deficiency can secondarily cause B12 deficiency.
  • Poultry show decreased egg production and hatchability.
  • Human deficiency causes pernicious anaemia.

posts.post_title: Choline deficiency leads to fatty liver beca…
posts.post_content: Choline deficiency leads to fatty liver because it is essential for which metabolic step?

_aimcq_options.text: Conversion of neutral fat to phospholipids in the liver
Absorption of dietary fat in the intestine

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Conversion of neutral fat to phospholipids in the liver

Choline deficiency impairs conversion of neutral fat into phospholipids in the liver, leading to fat accumulation (fatty liver).

Correct Option Explanation

Choline can be synthesised from the sulphur-containing amino acid methionine, and its deficiency contributes to fatty liver in pregnancy toxaemia of ewes.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Fat absorption is wrong — choline's key role is hepatic phospholipid conversion, not intestinal fat absorption.
  • Bile acid synthesis is wrong — this is not the mechanism described for choline's role in preventing fatty liver.
  • Beta-oxidation of ketones is wrong — this is unrelated to the described choline-phospholipid pathway.
Know More
  • Choline deficiency also contributes to perosis (slipped tendon) in poultry.
  • Rich sources include yeast and fish meal.
  • Fatty liver in pregnancy toxaemia of ewes is linked to reduced choline.
  • Choline works alongside other lipotropic factors in hepatic fat metabolism.

posts.post_title: Salt (Sodium/Chloride) deficiency leading to…
posts.post_content: Salt (Sodium/Chloride) deficiency leading to dehydration occurs through which sequence of events?

_aimcq_options.text: Reduced ECF osmotic pressure causes renal water reabsorption, reduced blood volume and haemoconcentration
Direct destruction of red blood cells

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Reduced ECF osmotic pressure causes renal water reabsorption, reduced blood volume and haemoconcentration

Salt deficiency reduces extracellular fluid (ECF) osmotic pressure, triggering renal water reabsorption, decreased blood volume and haemoconcentration.

Correct Option Explanation

This raises plasma protein and colloidal osmotic pressure, drawing water from interstitial fluid into capillaries, worsening tissue dehydration.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • RBC destruction is wrong — salt deficiency causes fluid shifts, not direct erythrocyte lysis.
  • Increased vitamin D activation is wrong — this is unrelated to sodium/chloride balance mechanisms.
  • Excess calcium mobilisation is wrong — this is a feature of calcium/phosphorus disorders, not sodium deficiency.
Know More
  • Sodium is mainly extracellular; chloride is both intra- and extracellular.
  • Heat exhaustion in working horses results from excess sweating and salt loss.
  • Poultry need 0.1–0.2% dietary salt.
  • Salt poisoning in poultry/pigs causes eosinophilic meningoencephalitis.

posts.post_title: Salt poisoning in swine characteristically p…
posts.post_content: Salt poisoning in swine characteristically produces which microscopic brain lesion?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Eosinophilic meningoencephalitis with perivascular cuffing

Salt poisoning in swine produces eosinophilic meningoencephalitis with perivascular cuffing by eosinophils and lymphocytes.

Correct Option Explanation

This occurs after excess salt intake with restricted water access, causing hyperaemia, oedema of the leptomeninges and neuronal degeneration.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Negri bodies is wrong — these are rabies viral inclusions, unrelated to salt toxicity.
  • Spongiform vacuolation is wrong — this describes prion diseases like Scrapie/BSE, not salt poisoning.
  • Demyelination is wrong — this is characteristic of lentiviral diseases like Visna, not salt toxicity.
Know More
  • Poultry salt poisoning shows ascites and visceral gout.
  • Swine causes include drinking brine or excess salted fish meal.
  • Chronic cases show somnolence, drooping ears and blindness.
  • Gastroenteritis is a gross lesion in acute swine cases.

posts.post_title: 'Milk fever' (Post-Parturient Paresis) in da…
posts.post_content: 'Milk fever' (Post-Parturient Paresis) in dairy cows is a sudden manifestation of which metabolic disturbance?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Hypocalcaemia

Milk fever is a sudden hypocalcaemia occurring at the onset of lactation, as maternal calcium is rapidly drained into milk.

Correct Option Explanation

Clinical signs include tetany, incoordination and unconsciousness, with the animal characteristically lying with its head turned toward the flank.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Hypomagnesaemia is wrong — this causes a related but distinct syndrome, 'grass tetany', not classic milk fever.
  • Hypokalaemia is wrong — potassium deficiency is not typically seen clinically in animals per this text.
  • Hyperphosphataemia is wrong — milk fever is specifically a calcium, not phosphorus, disturbance.
Know More
  • Low parathyroid activity contributes to the failure to maintain blood calcium.
  • It is most common in heavy milking cows.
  • Poultry show a related 'cage layer fatigue' with sudden paralysis.
  • Normal blood calcium is about 10–11 mg/100 ml.

posts.post_title: A phosphorus-deficient soil area in South Af…
posts.post_content: A phosphorus-deficient soil area in South Africa is associated with a syndrome ('Lamsiekte') where cattle develop depraved appetite and die from which secondary infection?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Clostridium botulinum (from chewing bones)

In Lamsiekte, phosphorus-deficient cattle develop pica and chew bones of dead animals, leading to fatal Clostridium botulinum toxin ingestion.

Correct Option Explanation

Phosphorus deficiency (aphosphorosis) also causes poor growth, lameness and reproductive disorders in affected cattle.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Clostridium tetani is wrong — this causes tetanus via wound infection, not the bone-chewing/botulism link of Lamsiekte.
  • Bacillus anthracis is wrong — anthrax is a septicaemic disease, unrelated to phosphorus-deficiency pica.
  • Clostridium chauvoei is wrong — this causes Black Quarter, a myonecrotic disease, not the botulism complication of Lamsiekte.
Know More
  • Aphosphorosis is endemic in phosphorus-poor soil areas.
  • Excess phosphorus in horses fed bran causes 'Miller's disease' (Bran's disease).
  • Renal disease causing phosphorus retention leads to 'renal rickets'.
  • Normal blood Ca:P ratio is approximately 2:1.

posts.post_title: 'Grass Tetany' (grass staggers) in pregnant/…
posts.post_content: 'Grass Tetany' (grass staggers) in pregnant/lactating cattle grazing lush pasture results from deficiency of which mineral?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Magnesium

Grass Tetany results from hypomagnesaemia in cattle grazing lush grass or young wheat shoots.

Correct Option Explanation

Contributing factors include poor magnesium absorption, increased ruminal ammonia, and high dietary potassium intake reducing magnesium uptake.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Calcium is wrong — calcium deficiency instead causes milk fever, a related but distinct hypocalcaemic syndrome.
  • Potassium is wrong — potassium deficiency is rarely seen clinically in animals; here it is a contributing factor, not the deficient mineral itself.
  • Sodium is wrong — sodium deficiency causes dehydration and salt-loss syndromes, not grass tetany.
Know More
  • Calves raised only on milk can develop hypomagnesaemia.
  • Pigs show a related 'stepping syndrome' with repeated hind limb lifting.
  • Normal magnesium level is about 2–3 mg/100 ml.
  • Mg:Ca ratio of 1:3.5 is needed for normal bone growth.

posts.post_title: Manganese deficiency in adult birds classica…
posts.post_content: Manganese deficiency in adult birds classically produces which slipped-tendon condition?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Perosis

Manganese deficiency in adult birds causes perosis, or slipped tendon, from failure of epiphyseal cartilage ossification.

Correct Option Explanation

Manganese is essential for cartilage matrix synthesis; deficiency also causes thin, porous eggshells and reduced hatchability in laying birds.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Curled toe paralysis is wrong — this is caused by riboflavin deficiency, not manganese.
  • Rickets is wrong — this is a vitamin D/calcium/phosphorus disorder, not manganese deficiency.
  • Osteomalacia is wrong — this adult bone-softening disease also relates to vitamin D/calcium, not manganese.
Know More
  • Rice bran is a good source of manganese.
  • Manganese works closely with magnesium in enzyme cofactor roles.
  • Young growing birds show chondrodystrophy with deficiency.
  • The gastrocnemius tendon slips in affected birds.

posts.post_title: Piglet anaemia, seen in baby pigs raised on…
posts.post_content: Piglet anaemia, seen in baby pigs raised on cement or wooden floors, results mainly from deficiency of which mineral?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Iron

Piglet anaemia is a microcytic hypochromic anaemia resulting from iron deficiency, since sow's milk is naturally low in iron.

Correct Option Explanation

Piglets normally obtain supplemental iron from soil contact; those raised on cement/wooden floors lack this source and develop anaemia by about 21 days of age.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Calcium is wrong — calcium deficiency causes bone disorders like rickets, not this anaemia pattern.
  • Magnesium is wrong — magnesium deficiency causes tetany syndromes, not piglet anaemia.
  • Zinc is wrong — zinc deficiency in pigs causes parakeratosis of skin, not anaemia.
Know More
  • Copper also aids iron absorption and is deficient similarly on hard floors.
  • Excess iron accumulation is called haemochromatosis.
  • Ferrous iron is more readily absorbed than ferric iron.
  • Phosphorus and phytic acid impair iron absorption by forming insoluble complexes.

posts.post_title: Copper deficiency in sheep in England and Au…
posts.post_content: Copper deficiency in sheep in England and Australia produces a neurological disease known as:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Enzootic ataxia (Sway back)

Copper deficiency in sheep produces Enzootic Ataxia, or 'Sway Back', with incoordination, hind limb weakness and demyelination of the cerebrum.

Correct Option Explanation

It occurs particularly when sheep graze molybdenum-rich pastures, since molybdenum is antagonistic to copper absorption.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Grass tetany is wrong — this is caused by magnesium deficiency, not copper.
  • Cerebrospinal nematodiasis is wrong — this is caused by aberrant Setaria digitata migration, a parasitic cause.
  • Scrapie is wrong — this is a prion disease, unrelated to copper nutrition.
Know More
  • Cattle show a related 'Falling disease' with sudden death and myocardial fibrosis.
  • Sheep wool loses colour and becomes hair-like ('steely wool').
  • Copper is required for cytochrome oxidase and haemoglobin synthesis.
  • Excess copper (e.g. CuSO4 drenching) causes gastritis and enteritis.

posts.post_title: Cobalt deficiency in ruminants causes anaemi…
posts.post_content: Cobalt deficiency in ruminants causes anaemia because cobalt is an essential constituent of which vitamin?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Vitamin B12

Cobalt is an essential constituent of Vitamin B12; its deficiency reduces ruminal microbial B12 synthesis, causing anaemia.

Correct Option Explanation

Affected ruminants show anorexia, pale mucous membranes, emaciation and fatty liver, known regionally as 'Pine' (England) or 'Enzootic marasmus' (Australia).

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Vitamin B1 is wrong — thiamine does not contain cobalt; it is unrelated to this mineral's deficiency syndrome.
  • Vitamin K is wrong — vitamin K is unrelated to cobalt and causes a haemorrhagic, not anaemic, syndrome when deficient.
  • Vitamin A is wrong — vitamin A deficiency causes epithelial keratinisation, not the cobalt-B12-linked anaemia.
Know More
  • The disease is called 'Hill sickness' in New Zealand.
  • In the USA it is termed 'Grand Traverse disease'.
  • Haemosiderosis is a described lesion of cobalt deficiency.
  • Cobalt comes from soil and plants grown in it.

posts.post_title: Parakeratosis in pigs, characterized by impe…
posts.post_content: Parakeratosis in pigs, characterized by imperfect keratinisation of skin, results from deficiency of which mineral, aggravated by excess dietary calcium?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Zinc

Parakeratosis in pigs is caused by zinc deficiency, aggravated by excess dietary calcium and phosphorus which interfere with zinc absorption.

Correct Option Explanation

Lesions include circumscribed erythematous areas on the abdomen and thighs due to imperfect keratinisation of the epidermis.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Iron is wrong — iron deficiency causes anaemia in piglets, not the skin lesion of parakeratosis.
  • Iodine is wrong — iodine deficiency causes goitre (thyroid enlargement), not skin keratinisation defects.
  • Manganese is wrong — manganese deficiency causes perosis (slipped tendon), not parakeratosis.
Know More
  • Cattle show parakeratosis and alopecia with zinc deficiency.
  • Sheep show wool loss with thick, wrinkled, crusted skin.
  • Poultry show poor feathering and scaly skin on legs.
  • Phytic acid and calcium form insoluble complexes with zinc.

posts.post_title: Iodine deficiency in animals classically man…
posts.post_content: Iodine deficiency in animals classically manifests as which condition?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Goitre (thyroid enlargement)

Iodine deficiency classically manifests as goitre, or enlargement of the thyroid gland.

Correct Option Explanation

It occurs in soil-deficient regions such as the Great Lakes, Alps and Himalayas, and can be worsened by goitrogenic feeds like soya bean meal.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Parakeratosis is wrong — this skin condition results from zinc deficiency, not iodine.
  • Fluorosis is wrong — this is caused by fluorine excess, the opposite nutritional problem, not iodine deficiency.
  • Rickets is wrong — this results from vitamin D/calcium/phosphorus imbalance, unrelated to iodine.
Know More
  • Iodine is a key component of thyroxine hormone.
  • Excess iodine intake ('Iodism') causes conjunctivitis and rhinitis.
  • Corn silage is cited as a goitrogenic substance.
  • Iodine deficiency areas correlate with specific mountainous/lake regions.

posts.post_title: Chronic Fluorosis in cattle characteristical…
posts.post_content: Chronic Fluorosis in cattle characteristically produces which dental change?

_aimcq_options.text: Mottled, chalk-like enamel with hypoplasia in lateral incisors

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Mottled, chalk-like enamel with hypoplasia in lateral incisors

Chronic Fluorosis produces mottled, chalk-like, opaque enamel with hypoplasia, especially in the lateral incisors of cattle.

Correct Option Explanation

Bones become shorter, thicker and more porous, with exostoses and susceptibility to fracture, from excess fluorine in soil, water or rock phosphate supplements.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Complete tooth loss is wrong — fluorosis produces enamel mottling and hypoplasia, not outright tooth loss.
  • Excessive tooth growth is wrong — this is not a described feature of fluorosis.
  • Green discolouration is wrong — the described colour change is chalky/mottled, not green.
Know More
  • Fluorosis threshold is around 2 ppm in water.
  • 'Shifting lameness' with anaemia occurs from haemopoietic suppression.
  • Acute poisoning may follow sodium fluoride use against ectoparasites.
  • Rock phosphate as a bone meal substitute can introduce excess fluorine.

posts.post_title: Selenium deficiency, along with vitamin E de…
posts.post_content: Selenium deficiency, along with vitamin E deficiency, causes which muscular condition also called White Muscle Disease?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Nutritional muscular dystrophy

Selenium deficiency, together with vitamin E deficiency, causes nutritional muscular dystrophy (White Muscle Disease).

Correct Option Explanation

Selenium is a component of glutathione peroxidase, an antioxidant enzyme; deficiency also causes pancreatic atrophy and reduced fat-soluble vitamin absorption.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Perosis is wrong — this is a manganese-deficiency slipped-tendon disorder, unrelated to selenium.
  • Grass tetany is wrong — this is a magnesium-deficiency syndrome, not selenium-related.
  • Parakeratosis is wrong — this skin disorder results from zinc deficiency, not selenium.
Know More
  • Chronic selenium excess causes 'Alkali disease' with hoof cracks ('Bob tail disease').
  • Acute selenium poisoning in cattle causes 'Blind staggers'.
  • Deficiency threshold is about 0.05 ppm in animal feed.
  • Poultry deficiency also causes exudative diathesis and encephalomalacia.

posts.post_title: Azoturia (Paralytic Myoglobinuria, 'Monday M…
posts.post_content: Azoturia (Paralytic Myoglobinuria, 'Monday Morning Sickness') in horses classically follows which precipitating event?

_aimcq_options.text: A few days of rest on full rations followed by exercise

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: A few days of rest on full rations followed by exercise

Azoturia classically follows a period of rest on full rations in working horses, followed by return to exercise.

Correct Option Explanation

Myofiber degeneration and necrosis occur with hyaline, fragmented fibres, and myoglobin casts cause renal tubular necrosis, giving brown ('port wine') urine.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Prolonged starvation is wrong — azoturia is linked to excess feed during rest, not starvation, which more relates to ketosis.
  • Vitamin E deficiency alone is wrong — while related muscle diseases exist from vitamin E deficiency, azoturia's trigger is rest-then-exercise on full rations.
  • Excess dietary calcium is wrong — this is not a described cause of azoturia.
Know More
  • Serum creatine kinase, ALP and AST are elevated.
  • Muscles show discoloured, haemorrhagic foci grossly.
  • Kidneys are swollen and congested.
  • The condition is also called paralytic myoglobinuria.

posts.post_title: Post-Parturient Haemoglobinuria in dairy cow…
posts.post_content: Post-Parturient Haemoglobinuria in dairy cows is an acute haemolytic anaemia whose pathogenesis is related to which metabolic disturbance?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Hypophosphataemia

Post-Parturient Haemoglobinuria is related to hypophosphataemia, occurring in multiparous cows a few weeks after calving.

Correct Option Explanation

Severe intravascular haemolysis drops red cell counts below 1 million/cmm, with Heinz bodies seen in erythrocytes and centrilobular hepatic necrosis.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Hypercalcaemia is wrong — this is linked to vitamin D excess, not the haemolytic anaemia of this postpartum condition.
  • Hyperkalaemia is wrong — potassium disturbances are not implicated in this specific disease.
  • Hypomagnesaemia is wrong — this instead underlies grass tetany, a different postpartum-associated metabolic disease.
Know More
  • Clinical signs include icterus, oedema and laboured breathing.
  • Lesions include haemoglobinuric nephropathy.
  • The disease is distinct from Bacillary Haemoglobinuria, which is infectious.
  • It typically affects cows that have calved several weeks previously.

posts.post_title: Ketosis in ruminants develops due to which u…
posts.post_content: Ketosis in ruminants develops due to which underlying metabolic shift?

_aimcq_options.text: Increased fatty acid oxidation compensating for hypoglycaemia, producing ketone bodies
Direct bacterial toxin production of ketones

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Increased fatty acid oxidation compensating for hypoglycaemia, producing ketone bodies

Ketosis develops when reduced glucose availability drives increased fatty acid oxidation, generating excess ketone bodies as an alternate energy source.

Correct Option Explanation

Inadequate oxaloacetate (needed for the TCA cycle) during active gluconeogenesis diverts acetyl-CoA toward ketogenesis instead.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Excess glucose utilisation is wrong — ketosis arises from glucose deficiency/hypoglycaemia, not excess utilisation.
  • Bacterial toxin production is wrong — ketone bodies are endogenous metabolic products, not bacterial toxins.
  • Excess protein catabolism alone is wrong — the core mechanism described is fat oxidation compensating for low glucose, not protein breakdown.
Know More
  • Ketone bodies are acetone, acetoacetic acid and beta-hydroxybutyric acid.
  • Diagnosis includes urinalysis and milk analysis for ketone bodies.
  • Hypoglycaemia is a defining biochemical feature.
  • Pregnancy and lactation are recognised precipitating causes.

posts.post_title: Pregnancy Toxaemia in ewes ('Pregnant Ewe Pa…
posts.post_content: Pregnancy Toxaemia in ewes ('Pregnant Ewe Paralysis') typically occurs in which stage of gestation and predisposing litter size?

_aimcq_options.text: Last weeks of pregnancy in ewes carrying twins or triplets
First trimester in ewes carrying a single lamb

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Last weeks of pregnancy in ewes carrying twins or triplets

Pregnancy Toxaemia occurs in the last weeks of pregnancy, typically in ewes carrying twins or triplets.

Correct Option Explanation

Toxic metabolic waste products from mother and fetuses, combined with dietary insufficiency causing ketosis/starvation, produce depression, sleepiness and coma.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • First trimester, single lamb is wrong — the disease specifically arises late in gestation with multiple fetuses, not early single-lamb pregnancy.
  • Immediately after weaning is wrong — this is unrelated to the described late-gestation timing of pregnancy toxaemia.
  • Mid-gestation in maiden ewes is wrong — the disease is linked to late gestation and multiple fetal burden, not mid-gestation in maidens.
Know More
  • Lesions include fatty change in liver, kidney and heart.
  • Terminal subepicardial petechiae and ecchymoses are described.
  • It is metabolically related to ketosis.
  • Depression progressing to coma is a hallmark clinical course.

posts.post_title: In lead poisoning, which haematological find…
posts.post_content: In lead poisoning, which haematological finding is a classic diagnostic indicator?

_aimcq_options.text: Basophilic stippling of red blood cells

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Basophilic stippling of red blood cells

Basophilic stippling of RBCs is a classic haematological indicator of lead poisoning, along with anisocytosis and polychromasia.

Correct Option Explanation

Blood or urinary aminolevulinic acid (ALA) and protoporphyrin levels are sensitive indicators, with ALA exceeding 500 mg/100 ml in poisoned animals.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Heinz bodies is wrong — these are associated with oxidative red cell damage, such as in Post-Parturient Haemoglobinuria, not lead poisoning.
  • Howell-Jolly bodies is wrong — these nuclear remnants are not the classic lead poisoning indicator described.
  • Target cells is wrong — these are not the diagnostic red cell change highlighted for lead toxicity in this text.
Know More
  • Normal blood lead level is about 0.05–0.25 ppm.
  • Blood lead of 0.35 ppm is diagnostic of poisoning.
  • Liver or kidney cortex lead at 10 ppm is diagnostically significant.
  • Anaemia is a common haematologic abnormality in lead toxicity.

posts.post_title: Dogs and cats are particularly susceptible t…
posts.post_content: Dogs and cats are particularly susceptible to mercury toxicity mainly from which source?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Mercurial ointments (via absorption and licking)

Dogs and cats are particularly susceptible to mercury toxicity from mercurial ointments, through both direct skin absorption and licking of treated areas.

Correct Option Explanation

Organic mercurial poisoning produces delayed CNS signs including cerebellar ataxia, hypermetria and tremors, especially notable in cats.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Contaminated fish is wrong — while fish bioaccumulate methylmercury, ointment exposure is the specific route emphasised for dogs and cats.
  • Industrial vapour inhalation is wrong — this route is more relevant to sheep and cattle exposure to mercury vapour.
  • Vaccination residues is wrong — this is not a described source of mercury toxicity in this text.
Know More
  • Inorganic mercurial poisoning causes gastroenteritis and acute nephritis.
  • Organic mercurial poisoning has a delayed latent period of weeks.
  • Cerebellar Purkinje cell damage occurs in organic mercury poisoning.
  • Mercury bioaccumulates up to 300-fold in fish.

posts.post_title: Chronic copper poisoning in sheep progresses…
posts.post_content: Chronic copper poisoning in sheep progresses to a fatal 'haemolytic crisis' stage characterized by which findings?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Generalized icterus, haemoglobinaemia and haemoglobinuria

The haemolytic crisis stage of chronic copper poisoning shows generalized icterus, haemoglobinaemia and haemoglobinuria, lasting 2–5 days before death.

Correct Option Explanation

The liver becomes enlarged, yellow and friable, with the spleen showing dark 'blackberry jam' parenchyma from massive haemolysis.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Bone fragility and mottled teeth is wrong — these are features of chronic fluorosis, not copper poisoning.
  • Cerebellar ataxia and tremors is wrong — this describes organic mercury toxicity, not the copper haemolytic crisis.
  • Papillary muscle necrosis alone is not the defining finding of the copper haemolytic crisis, which centres on haemolysis and icterus.
Know More
  • Kidneys appear 'gunmetal' coloured with haemorrhagic mottling.
  • Faeces are deep green from a copper-chlorophyll compound in acute poisoning.
  • Low dietary molybdenum enhances hepatic copper storage.
  • Liver copper >150 ppm (wet weight) is diagnostically significant in sheep.

posts.post_title: Nitrite poisoning causes cyanosis and chocol…
posts.post_content: Nitrite poisoning causes cyanosis and chocolate-brown blood discolouration through which mechanism?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Conversion of haemoglobin to methaemoglobin

Nitrite poisoning converts haemoglobin to methaemoglobin, which cannot carry oxygen, causing cyanosis and chocolate-brown blood.

Correct Option Explanation

Nitrite ions can also cross the placenta and convert fetal haemoglobin to methaemoglobin, inducing abortion in pregnant animals.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Direct haemolysis is wrong — nitrite toxicity works through methaemoglobin formation, not direct erythrocyte lysis.
  • Carboxyhaemoglobin formation is wrong — this occurs in carbon monoxide poisoning, not nitrite toxicity.
  • Clotting factor depletion is wrong — nitrite poisoning does not primarily act through coagulation factor loss; blood clots poorly but this is secondary.
Know More
  • Pigs are most susceptible to nitrite poisoning.
  • Ruminants convert plant nitrate to nitrite via rumen microflora.
  • Diagnosis includes the diphenylamine spot test for nitrate.
  • Response to methylene blue treatment supports diagnosis.

posts.post_title: In Salmonellosis, the small aggregations of…
posts.post_content: In Salmonellosis, the small aggregations of reticulo-endothelial cells forming discrete foci in the liver are called:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Paratyphoid nodules

Paratyphoid nodules are small reticulo-endothelial cell aggregates found in the liver in Salmonellosis.

Correct Option Explanation

Salmonella invades intestinal epithelium via fimbriae, proliferates within enterocytes and macrophages, and can produce septicaemia or enteritis.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Koch's blue bodies is wrong — these are Theileria schizonts in lymphocytes, unrelated to Salmonella.
  • Negri bodies is wrong — these are rabies viral inclusions in neurons, unrelated to bacterial hepatic nodules.
  • Sulphur granules is wrong — these are organism colonies seen in Actinomycosis/Actinobacillosis, not Salmonellosis.
Know More
  • Septicaemic form is characteristic in newborn foals, calves and guinea pigs.
  • Mortality in acute enteritis form can reach 75%.
  • Ulcerative proctitis occurs in enterocolitis.
  • Abortion occurs late in gestation with oedematous, necrotic placenta.

posts.post_title: Enterotoxic colibacillosis, most common in y…
posts.post_content: Enterotoxic colibacillosis, most common in young piglets, calves and lambs in the first week of life, is characterized by which pathogenic mechanism?

_aimcq_options.text: Colonisation of intestinal cells by E. coli with toxin production
Bacterial penetration into mesenteric lymph nodes
Destruction of villi without toxin production

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Colonisation of intestinal cells by E. coli with toxin production

Enterotoxic colibacillosis results from E. coli colonisation of the intestinal surface with local toxin production, without deep tissue invasion.

Correct Option Explanation

This mechanism differs from enteroinvasive colibacillosis, where the organism penetrates enterocytes, lamina propria and mesenteric lymph nodes.

Incorrect Options Analysis
  • Penetration into mesenteric lymph nodes is wrong — this describes enteroinvasive colibacillosis, a distinct pathogenic type.
  • Destruction of villi without toxin is wrong — this describes enteroadherent colibacillosis, which lacks toxin production.
  • Systemic septicaemia without diarrhoea is wrong — this describes septicaemic colibacillosis, a different pattern.
Know More
  • Enteroadherent colibacillosis destroys microvilli by adhesion, without toxin.
  • Oedema Disease is a form of enterotoxaemic colibacillosis.
  • Septicaemic colibacillosis causes polyserositis without diarrhoea.
  • E. coli fimbriae mediate attachment to intestinal epithelial cells.

posts.post_title: Contagious Pleuropneumonia of Swine, caused…
posts.post_content: Contagious Pleuropneumonia of Swine, caused by Haemophilus pleuropneumoniae, produces which characteristic lung lesion?

posts.post_title: Infectious Thrombo-Embolic Meningoencephalit…
posts.post_content: Infectious Thrombo-Embolic Meningoencephalitis of cattle is caused by which organism?

posts.post_title: In ringworm (dermatophytosis), which genus g…
posts.post_content: In ringworm (dermatophytosis), which genus grows around the hair root forming a mosaic spore pattern (ectothrix) and fluoresces under UV light?

Microsporum fungi grow around the hair root in a mosaic ectothrix pattern and fluoresce under UV (Wood's lamp) light.

posts.post_title: Favus, the 'honeycomb ringworm', is caused m…
posts.post_content: Favus, the 'honeycomb ringworm', is caused mainly by which fungal species?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:

Favus, the 'honeycomb ringworm', is caused mainly by Trichophyton schoenleinii, along with Microsporum gypseum and M. gallinae.

posts.post_title: Epizootic Lymphangitis of horses, mules and…
posts.post_content: Epizootic Lymphangitis of horses, mules and donkeys is caused by which organism, indistinguishable from Histoplasma capsulatum in tissue?

posts.post_title: Cryptococcosis, caused by Cryptococcus neofo…
posts.post_content: Cryptococcosis, caused by Cryptococcus neoformans, characteristically affects which two organ systems?

posts.post_title: Zygomycosis (Phycomycosis) differs microscop…
posts.post_content: Zygomycosis (Phycomycosis) differs microscopically from other deep mycoses in that its tissue reaction is:

_aimcq_options.text: Diffuse and pyogranulomatous rather than forming classical granulomas
Purely granulomatous with Langhans giant cells

  • Purely granulomatous with Langhans cells is wrong — this classical pattern is more typical of histoplasmosis or coccidioidomycosis, not zygomycosis.

posts.post_title: Histoplasmosis is caused by Histoplasma caps…
posts.post_content: Histoplasmosis is caused by Histoplasma capsulatum, which grows in which form within the host body at 37°C?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Yeast cell form

Histoplasma capsulatum grows as a yeast cell at body temperature (37°C) and in culture at that temperature, but as a mycelium in soil at room temperature.

  • Mycelial form is wrong — this growth form occurs in the soil at room temperature, not within the host.
  • Spherule form is wrong — this thick-walled reproductive structure describes Coccidioides immitis, not Histoplasma.

Know More
  • Dogs are most often affected among domestic animals.

posts.post_title: Coccidioidomycosis is caused by Coccidioides…

Coccidioides immitis produces distinctive spherules (sporangia) with a double-contoured wall, ranging from 5–50 microns in diameter.

  • Pseudohyphae is wrong — this structure is characteristic of Candida infections, not Coccidioides.

posts.post_content: Immature Amphistomiasis (stomach fluke disease), unlike infection by mature flukes, is pathogenic because immature flukes:

posts.post_title: Schistosoma nasale causes 'snoring disease'…
posts.post_content: Schistosoma nasale causes 'snoring disease' in cattle by residing in the veins of which anatomical site?

Schistosoma nasale resides in the veins of the nasal mucosa of cattle and buffalo, causing nasal granuloma or 'snoring disease'.

posts.post_title: In E. coli tropism, which pilus type binds s…
posts.post_content: In E. coli tropism, which pilus type binds sialic acid and causes meningitis?

Type S pili of E. coli bind sialic acid host receptors and are associated with causing meningitis.

posts.post_title: Which bacterial virulence factor allows Baci…
posts.post_content: Which bacterial virulence factor allows Bacillus anthracis to resist phagocytosis by neutrophils?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: The capsule

The capsule of Bacillus anthracis allows it to resist phagocytosis by neutrophils and inhibits action of the reticuloendothelial system.

The capsule also has fibrinolytic properties that prevent blood clotting, contributing to the organism's ability to spread through tissues.

  • Flagella is wrong — B. anthracis is a non-motile organism and flagella are not its key virulence factor.

  • Anthrax toxin has three factors: oedema, protective antigen and lethal factors.

posts.post_title: Colonisation resistance, a defence mechanism…
posts.post_content: Colonisation resistance, a defence mechanism against bacterial attachment, works primarily through which process?

Correct Answer: Normal microflora occupying or blocking receptor sites and producing bacteriocins

Colonisation resistance works through normal microflora occupying or blocking receptor sites and producing toxic metabolites and bacteriocins.

  • Complement lysis is wrong — this is a distinct innate immune mechanism, not the microflora-based colonisation resistance described.

posts.post_title: In FMD, which secondary/sequelae effect is l…
posts.post_content: In FMD, which secondary/sequelae effect is linked to endocrine damage, especially of the thyroid gland?

posts.post_title: In Rinderpest pathogenesis, the destruction…
posts.post_content: In Rinderpest pathogenesis, the destruction of lymphocytes in lymphoid organs is directly responsible for which haematological finding?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Marked leucopoenia

Rinderpest virus's affinity for lymphoid tissue causes pronounced lymphocyte destruction, directly producing marked leucopoenia.

This immunosuppression from lymphoid destruction also predisposes affected cattle to activation of latent parasitic or bacterial infections.

  • Thrombocytosis is wrong — an increase in platelets is not a described feature; leucopoenia is the hallmark change.
